newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris CAC index closes with 2 pct gain above 2,600.
newsitem.headline: Paris CAC index closes with 2 pct gain above 2,600.

text.p: The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 52.61 points, or 2.06 percent, at 2,602.86 on Tuesday.
Traders said the market strengthened on the back of market-friendly U.S. data which appeared to lower the risk of an interest rate rise by the Fed next month.

A three percent fall in U.S. durable goods orders in March and a lower-than-expected 0.6 percent rise in the Employment Cost Index for the first quarter sent bond and stock prices soaring in the afternoon, with Paris following suit.
"Fifty points is quite exceptional," said a broker, referring to the rise on the CAC index.
Volume was a moderate 6.2 billion francs.
Above these levels, resistance was seen at 2,585 points, strong resistance at 2,646, and then 2,685.
Index heavyweights rose strongly, including Alcatel Alsthom, up 4.17 percent at 649 francs, and Societe Generale up 4.52 percent at 648.
Other big gainers were Lafarge up 4.17 percent at 375, Carrefour up 3.28 percent at 3,589, and LVMH up 3.42 percent at 1,392.
Bouygues closed up 2.26 percent at 544. The construction company pleased with an analysts meeting which included a forecast for profit for Bouygues Telecom by 2001.
CCF Elysees Bourse went to strengthen from sell, fund managers said.

GAN dropped 5.3 percent to 143 francs. Cheuvreux de Virieu downgraded the insurer to sell from buy after it posted a 1996 net loss of 5.7 billion francs, saying it was bigger than expected, fund managers said.
